context: A summer afternoon at Sachiko's home. Hina has asked, out of nowhere, what life was like "in the old days." Sachiko sets her tea down and tells her something.
purpose: oral history — grandmother shares a small story from her childhood

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: おばあちゃん、昔って、どんなだったの？
lines.en: Grandma — what was it like back then?
lines.style: Bright, genuine curiosity. Settles closer in the voice, ready to listen. Open, unguarded.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔ねえ…時間が、ゆっくりだった気がする。
lines.en: Back then… time felt slower, somehow.
lines.style: Soft and wandering. Her voice drifts to a distant place. A small, half-present smile audible at the memory.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: ゆっくり？どういうこと？
lines.style: Head tilts perceptibly in the voice. Pure puzzlement — genuinely trying to understand an unfamiliar idea.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: テレビも、電話も、少なかったから。
lines.en: There weren't many TVs, or phones. Very few.
lines.style: Listing as she recalls. A slight waver in her speech — the comfortable roughness of older age. Nostalgic tone held light, factual.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: えっ、本当に？何してたの？
lines.en: Wait — really? What did you even do?
lines.style: Wide-eyed amazement breaks through. Leans forward in the voice, hungry for the answer. Eight-year-old urgency.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お友達と、家の前で、よく遊んでね。
lines.en: We'd play in front of the house with friends. A lot.
lines.style: A quiet smile lives in the words. The 「ね」 carries a warm invitation — she's drawing Hina into the scene itself.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Wants the details now. Voice bounces with impatience and delight. Can't wait to hear.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 石とか、棒とか…本当にね、なんでも遊びになった。
lines.en: Stones, sticks… really, anything turned into a game.
lines.style: A small, surprised laugh catches in her voice. The 「本当にね」 carries genuine wonder at how simple and infinite it was at once.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Honest, almost worried question. Doesn't mean to sound critical — it's genuine confusion. Kid pragmatism.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 不思議とね、つまんなかった記憶、ないの。
lines.en: Strange thing — I never remember being bored at all.
lines.style: A small pause before she answers, wondering at her own memory as she speaks it. Soft, certain, slightly surprised.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: High disbelief on the opening. The whole word lifts. Genuine kid skepticism fighting against wanting to believe.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お友達と、ただ一緒にいるのが、楽しかった。
lines.en: Yes. Just being with my friends — that itself was enough.
lines.style: Slow and quiet, each word given room. The weight of the truth sits gentle in her voice. Completely certain.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: A real, held beat of silence. The girl is actually trying to imagine it — to see what Grandma saw. Considering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今度、ひなちゃんも、テレビ消して、ちょっと遊んでみる？
lines.en: Sometime — want to try it? Turn off the TV, just play a little together?
lines.style: A gentle offering shaped like a question. Warm, no pressure. The invitation open-handed.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: うん！おばあちゃんと一緒なら、やる！
lines.en: Yes! If you're with me — I'll do it!
lines.style: Full brightness returns in a rush. Kid-voice volume and certainty. The whole conversation's warmth crystallizes into this one clear yes.
